title: Excavator Operator Salary: Award Rates, Casual Loading, and Annual Pay Guide
description: Learn how to calculate an excavator operator salary from award rates, including casual loading, super, and tax. Use our hourly to annual conversion guide.
salarySummary: The minimum hourly rate for an excavator operator under the Building and Construction General On-site Award is around $29.45 to $30.38 per hour for a 38-hour week, depending on classification, with casual loading adding 25%.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for an excavator operator under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Building and Construction General On-site Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate for a Level 3 employee (CW/ECW 3) is $29.45, and for Level 4 (CW/ECW 4) it is $30.38, based on the 2026 rates published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. The actual classification depends on the specific duties and skills required, so you should check the award definitions or use the Pay and Conditions Tool.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to an excavator operator salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate as compensation for entitlements like annual leave and paid sick leave. For example, a Level 4 casual excavator operator would be paid $30.38 × 1.25 = $37.98 per hour. This loading is included in the ordinary hourly rate for calculating overtime and penalty rates, as per the award.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for an excavator operator?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of the gross pay at the current super guarantee rate of 12% of ordinary time earnings. For a full-time excavator operator earning $30.38 per hour for 38 hours a week, the annual super contribution would be $30.38 × 38 × 52 × 0.12 = $7,203.71, subject to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is an employer obligation and does not reduce the employee's take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Excavator Operator Salary Under the Award

Excavator operators in Australia are typically covered by the Building and Construction General On-site Award 2020 (MA000020). The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides that set minimum hourly rates for different classification levels. Based on the 2026 award rates, a Level 3 employee (CW/ECW 3) earns a minimum of $29.45 per hour, while a Level 4 employee (CW/ECW 4) earns $30.38 per hour. These rates include the industry allowance and tool allowance where applicable. The exact classification for an excavator operator depends on the complexity of the work and the operator's skills, so you should refer to the award's classification definitions or use the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database.

## How to Calculate Annual Pay from Hourly Rate

To estimate an annual excavator operator salary, use the standard formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week (the standard under the award), the calculation is straightforward. For example, at the Level 4 rate of $30.38 per hour:

- Annual: $30.38 × 38 × 52 = $60,030.88
- Fortnightly: $30.38 × 38 × 2 = $2,308.88

This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you have a different hourly rate, you can use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see the annual equivalent.

## Casual Loading and Its Effect on Pay

Many construction workers are engaged as casuals. The award requires a 25% casual loading on the base hourly rate for all ordinary hours worked. This loading compensates for entitlements such as annual leave, personal leave, and public holidays not worked. For a casual excavator operator at Level 4:

- Casual hourly rate: $30.38 × 1.25 = $37.98
- Annual casual pay: $37.98 × 38 × 52 = $75,048.48

Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply the loading correctly. Remember, the loading is added to the base rate, not the other way around.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% on ordinary time earnings. This is paid on top of the gross salary, so it does not reduce take-home pay. For a full-time permanent excavator operator earning $60,030.88 per year, the super contribution would be $7,203.71 (12% of $60,030.88), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For casual employees, super is calculated on the gross pay including the casual loading. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for more details.

## Tax on Your Excavator Operator Salary

Income tax is deducted from your gross pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). Using the Level 4 annual salary of $60,030.88:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 - $18,200) × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $60,030.88: ($60,030.88 - $45,000) × 30% = $4,509.26
- Total tax: $8,529.26
- Medicare levy: $60,030.88 × 2% = $1,200.62
- Total deductions: $9,729.88
- Estimated take-home pay: $50,301.00 per year

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

## Distinguishing Award Rates from the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates for construction workers are higher because they include industry-specific allowances. For example, the Level 3 award rate of $29.45 is about 11% above the national minimum. Always check the relevant award or enterprise agreement to ensure you are paid correctly. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details.

## Fortnightly Pay in Construction

Many construction employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by 76 (38 hours × 2 weeks). For a casual at $37.98 per hour, that's $2,886.48 per fortnight before tax and super. This can help with budgeting and comparing job offers.

## Using Pay Guides and Reference Tables

The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, including the Building and Construction General On-site Award. These guides summarise minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database offers detailed classification data. You can also use our [reference tables](/data) to compare different award rates.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay estimates are based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. They assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
